constraints.notes: First-cut imperfect-hardware removable-media fallback; host keeps attach and mount authority, probes the medium with fstyp, admits only a small reviewed filesystem-family set, requires ro/nosuid/noexec/nosymfollow/untrusted, treats the mounted tree as inert input only, keeps the ingest walk physical and root-pinned, admits only regular files plus explicit directories, fails closed on symlink/device/FIFO/socket semantics, does not preserve hardlink topology in the first cut, member paths normalize to relative-clean Unicode NFC text, normalization collisions fail closed, there is no silent auto-rename or source-prefix repair, and the ingest jail receives a mounted tree instead of raw block device nodes, keeps path/kind/payload-first reviewed/import identity, keeps owner/mode/mtime/xattr fidelity out of scope in the first cut, and treats any receiver-local metadata outcomes as receiver-local realization detail rather than portable reviewed state. This first lane stays single-selected-subject only, the selected subject stays regular-file-only in the first cut, directories are not selectable import subjects in this lane, and direct multi-member review/import is out of scope in the first cut. Approval in this first lane stays present-device-instance-only, physical detach or lease end revokes it, and reattaching the same nominal medium requires a fresh grant even when serial or disk-ident hints look the same. The canonical attach receipt for this lane keeps a finite current-presence hint bundle (`ugen`/provider plus disk-ident or physical-path hints when available), explicitly marks those hints evidence-only, and keeps same-hints-on-reattach non-authoritative. Once one selected regular file is chosen, the first non-browsing step is capture-first into disposable /work staging, later operations do not consume the live mounted /ingest path, and capture failure or digest mismatch fails closed. after capture verifies against the planned subject digest, that exact captured subject must commit into authoritative quarantine store before detach. after that commit, the host should end the removable-medium session, emit device.detach.receipt, and do so before later classify/scan/sanitize work continues. later work then restarts in a fresh post-detach worker with /ingest absent and with no inherited file-descriptor/current-working-directory/root references to the old mount, and those later operations read a read-only projection of the stored preserved capture rather than the old scratch path. After verified capture and detach, the exact captured subject remains preserved evidence in authoritative quarantine store, later classify/scan/sanitize work may not rewrite that capture in place, and any sanitized output is a separate derivative from the preserved capture. After detach, later work receives only a single-object synthetic projection of the stored preserved capture; the authoritative quarantine-store locator remains receipt-visible evidence and the later worker may not browse the store namespace. That worker-visible delivery is only synthetic plumbing, must bind to the same preserved selected subject digest before later operations begin, and the canonical receipt must record that digest-bound continuity explicitly. After detach, later delivery stays launcher-preopened read-only (or equivalent), any worker-visible path is compatibility-only plumbing over that already-bound object, and the later worker must not reopen the preserved subject through broader path or store lookup. Any receipt-visible derivative output must leave through launcher-precreated disposable sink objects, any worker outbox path remains non-authoritative execution plumbing, the first lane admits only one declared writable derivative slot, extra worker result surface stays out, and the launcher/broker must collect + remeasure the bytes from that declared slot before the receipt names an authoritative derivative locator. The launcher/broker must still collect + remeasure those bytes before the receipt names an authoritative derivative locator. The one declared writable derivative slot starts as a launcher-precreated empty regular file, the launcher hands it to the later worker already opened O_APPEND, keeps it append-only-protected while the worker runs, omits CAP_READ/CAP_FTRUNCATE/CAP_FCNTL from worker authority, and treats any CAP_SEEK on that seekable file as implementation ballast rather than rewrite authority, so derivative egress stays append-open with no worker readback or truncate. The launcher or its approved shim must enter capability mode before handing control to later classify/scan/sanitize tool code, descendants inherit that mode and may not clear it, no ambient absolute-path opens remain after cap_enter, and any tool that cannot run on the preopened capability set stays out of this first lane unless a later explicit wrapper/broker contract earns it. Before later tool mainline begins, the launcher must close or spawn-closefrom every non-reviewed descriptor, the reviewed post-detach set stays closed-world, stdin stays inert null/empty input only, stdout/stderr stay launcher-owned observation channels or reviewed append-only log sinks, and no parent TTY/session socket is inherited into this first lane. The post-detach later worker also starts with reviewed-minimal-env-no-inherited-parent-env, launcher-reviewed-argv-no-media-derived-args, and launcher-owned-empty-workdir-no-ingest-store-cwd: the launcher builds a reviewed minimal environment rather than inheriting the parent environment, uses launcher-reviewed argv rather than media-derived arguments, and sets cwd to launcher-owned empty scratch instead of /ingest, the store, or parent cwd. Post-detach executable identity is launcher-resolved and digest-pinned (launcher-resolved-executable-digest-no-path-search); no PATH/cwd/media-derived executable lookup is admitted, receipts must record executable and wrapper digests (receipt-records-executable-and-wrapper-digests), and implicit helper/plugin discovery stays out (no-implicit-helper-or-plugin-discovery). Post-detach worker credentials are launcher-fixed and unprivileged (launcher-fixed-unprivileged-credential-envelope-no-supplementary-groups); receipts record the worker credential envelope (receipt-records-worker-credential-envelope), the worker runs as derive-rm-worker:derive-rm-worker, supplementary groups are absent (no-supplementary-groups), and setuid/setgid/saved-id or ambient privilege regain is unavailable (no-setuid-setgid-saved-id-or-ambient-privilege-regain). Post-detach worker lifecycle is launcher-supervised and daemon-free (launcher-supervised-no-daemon-or-orphan-descendants); no background descendants or unreviewed subprocesses may outlive the reviewed worker (no-background-descendants-or-unreviewed-subprocesses), and the launcher must reap the entire worker tree before derivative receipt authority (launcher-reaps-entire-worker-tree-before-receipt, receipt-records-worker-exit-and-descendant-reap). Post-detach later workers also stay inside a launcher-enforced resource envelope: CPU time, wall clock, memory, open files, process count, scratch bytes, and declared derivative-output bytes are bounded, receipt-visible, and resource-limit hits fail closed without derivative authority. Post-detach peer interaction is launcher-isolated too: launcher-isolated-peer-envelope-no-ambient-ptrace-signal-or-ipc, receipt-records-peer-isolation-and-signal-policy, launcher-only-signal-control-no-peer-or-session-control, no-unreviewed-ipc-sockets-shm-pipes-or-procfs, and procfs-ptrace-and-ktrace-unavailable-to-worker-and-peers; ambient same-UID peer control, ptrace/procfs/ktrace visibility, unreviewed IPC, session signals, and operator shell attachment stay out of the first lane. Post-detach network egress stays absent and receipt-visible; DNS/NSS, proxy configuration, remote fetches, and callbacks do not become derivative authority in the first lane. Persistent state stays `persistent-state-absent-no-home-cache-or-host-state-writes`; receipts must record `receipt-records-persistent-state-absence-and-scratch-cleanup`, scratch stays `launcher-created-empty-scratch-nonauthoritative` and `scratch-destroyed-before-derivative-receipt`, and `no-user-home-cache-config-or-history-state` keeps user-home/cache/config/history state out of ordinary derivative authority. FreeBSD r536 correction: Linux-style nodev is not treated as a FreeBSD mount flag; device-node denial is enforced by devfs/no-raw-device posture plus regular-file-only capture.
